subject.title: Feature: Postcondition checks for cron jobs (deterministic verification of agent outcomes)

question: Should cron post-run verification be implemented as a scheduler-owned bounded verifier contract, a plugin-owned fail-capable hook, or deferred until a broader agent-verification API exists?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the proposed verifier changes command execution, retry semantics, persisted state, protocol, UI/CLI, plugin hooks, and security boundaries that automation should not choose by itself.

options.title: Approve bounded scheduler contract
options.body: Define a typed post-run verifier owned by cron, with explicit command or plugin adapters, timeouts, output caps, redaction, persisted status, retry limits, and failure-alert integration.

options.title: Add plugin seam first
options.body: Add a fail-capable cron post-run hook that can return pass, fail, retry, or escalate decisions while keeping verifier implementation outside core.

options.title: Defer verification API
options.body: Keep this issue as a design tracker until maintainers settle a broader agent outcome-verification architecture across cron and outbound hooks.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded scheduler contract
recommendation.body: Define a typed post-run verifier owned by cron, with explicit command or plugin adapters, timeouts, output caps, redaction, persisted status, retry limits, and failure-alert integration.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact cron postcondition gap and is the listed project owner for product/security boundary decisions.
